title: Days of the Week
story: Your alarm clock app needs different behaviors for weekdays (loud alarm!) versus weekends (snooze mode!). You need a foolproof way to tell Saturday from Monday.
why: Enums are perfect for days of the week — a small, well-known, fixed set. This lesson reinforces match with a relatable, everyday example.
analogy: An enum for days is like a wall calendar — the days are printed, immutable, and you can't add an eighth day no matter how hard you try.
try_it: Write a `mood` function that returns an emoji description for each day: Monday = "tired", Friday = "excited", Saturday = "happy", Sunday = "relaxed". Use match to return all seven.
tips: Use `|` to group many variants: `Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday => "weekday"`
Match is exhaustive — if you define 7 variants, you need 7 arms (or groupings that cover all 7)
Enums can be returned from functions: `fn next_day(day: Day) -> Day` returns another enum value
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle all 7 days in a match — the compiler will remind you, but check your logic
Writing days as strings: `"Monday"` instead of `Day.Monday` — they look similar but are different types
Using `Monday..Friday` range syntax — XIOM doesn't support enum ranges; list each variant or use `|`
